previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with a history of CNS diffuse large B-cell lymphoma was admitted for scheduled maintenance chemotherapy with high-dose methotrexate. He tolerated the infusion well, with methotrexate levels declining appropriately to 0.13 by discharge, indicating effective clearance. He remained stable throughout the admission, with no significant complications. Mild transaminitis was noted, likely due to methotrexate, and was expected to resolve. His chronic conditions, including diabetes insipidus and hypertension, were managed without issue. He reported intermittent upper abdominal and chest discomfort, deemed non-cardiac and likely due to gas or muscle spasm, with follow-up recommended post-discharge. He was discharged home with instructions to complete a short course of leucovorin and sodium bicarbonate, continue his regular medications, and resume rituximab and temozolomide when insurance coverage allows. The next chemotherapy cycle is scheduled in four months.
problems: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, extranodal and solid organ sites
Presence of artificial hip joint, bilateral

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo male with a history of CNS lymphoma admitted for scheduled 
chemotherapy with methotrexate.  He tolerated treatment well 
without significant side affect. Notably, he did report 
increasing facial paresthesias and right hand numbness. We 
obtained a bedside EEG. Preliminary read is negative. We also 
sent a lamotrigine level; the results are still pending. He will 
need to have repeat head MRI and clinic appointment next week to 
follow these issues up. Presuming no new issues are found, his 
next treatment would be in 6 months on ___.

# CNS Lymphoma: Currently in remission. Most recent imaging on 
___ without evidence of recurrence. Received rituximab on 
___. Urine was alklanized per protocol with sodium bicarbonate 
IV and po. He received 8g/m2 HD-MTX on ___ and tolerated 
treatment well. Leucovorin was started per protocol and MTX 
levels were trended every 24 hours. On discharge, level was 
0.13, so he was provided with leucovorin and sodium bicarbonate 
po to take for 24 hours at home. He also restarted 240mg daily 
of temozolamide, which he will take for 7 days with HD-MTX 
treatment. 

Of note, given his new paresthesias in face and right hand, do 
have some concern about recurrent disease. Recommended obtaining 
MRI prior to discharge, but patient had prior plans he wished to 
keep, and requested discharge home. Will have him follow up in 
clinic next week with MRI.

# Seizure disorder: Patient reported facial paresthesias and 
right hand numbness. Symptoms concerning partial seizures vs 
recurrent CNS disease. Bedside EEG was obtained, preliminary 
report negative. We also sent lamotrigine level, which is still 
pending. We continued his current lamotrigine dose. He will also 
need repeat MRI next week with his outpatient appointment with 
Dr. ___.

# Diabetes insipidus: Continued home vasopressin. Monitored Na 
daily
 
# HTN: Held lisinopril while in house. Continued home 
propranolol prn for anxiety.

# Anxiety: Continued home propranolol.

# Billing: >30 minutes spent coordinating and executing this 
discharge plan.
